title: Sharp threshold for a one-dimensional thin film equation in the supercritical case
summary: We study a one-dimensional thin film equation combining competitive effects of aggregation and repulsion, where repulsion is modeled by fourth-order diffusion and aggregation by backward second-order degenerate diffusion with exponent $m>0$. Under natural regularity constraints, we prove that for every $m>0$, there exists a unique (up to the mass-critical case $m=3$) nonnegative, radially decreasing steady state $U_*$ which coincides with the extremal function of the sharp Sz.-Nagy inequality and is simultaneously the global minimizer of the free energy.
